Many mammals, such as elephants and primates, display intricate communication systems and social hierarchies that facilitate cooperation and survival. tasks.passage: The Erie Canal, completed in 1825, is a historic waterway in the United States that linked the Atlantic Ocean to the Great Lakes. tasks.title: Sleep And Memory 睡眠与记忆（4/5 ❌错1）
tasks.passage: Sleep is not merely a passive period of rest; it plays an active role in the consolidation of memory, a process that has been extensively examined by neuroscientists over several decades. During sleep, distinct stages—most notably rapid-eye-movement (REM) sleep and deep sleep—contribute in different ways to how memories are stored and organized. Experimental research suggests that while REM sleep strengthens emotionally charged memories, deep sleep supports the retention of factual knowledge and the acquisition of skills. Some researchers further propose that sleep functions as a kind of neural 'data management' system. [A] While awake, the brain continuously forms new connections as it processes incoming information, creating a dense and potentially inefficient network. [B] During sleep, however, unnecessary connections are trimmed, whereas essential ones are reinforced, [C] a reorganization that enhances the brain's ability to retrieve information accurately. [D] Not surprisingly, sleep deprivation has been shown to impair memory retention and conceptual integration. Even a single night of lost sleep can reduce recall and interfere with learning. Nevertheless, studies also indicate that recovery sleep—particularly when it is deep and uninterrupted—can partially reverse these effects, suggesting that although sleep is critical for memory, the brain retains a limited capacity to adapt to disruption.

tasks.title: Sports Social Integration 体育与社会融合（3/5 ❌错2）
tasks.passage: Sports can promote social integration by bridging gaps between people of various backgrounds. Participation in sports can lead to increased social cohesion and improved relationships among diverse groups. For example, community soccer leagues often bring together people from different ethnicities, creating an environment where cultural differences are celebrated and mutual respect is cultivated. However, the impact of sports on social integration is not without challenges. Competitive environments can sometimes exacerbate social tensions, particularly when favoritism or exclusionary practices are present. Despite these issues, many initiatives aim to use sports as a platform for social change. One such initiative is the Sport for Peace program, which focuses on conflict resolution through team-building activities and collaborative sports events. The role of sports in social integration extends beyond participation. Spectatorship and fandom also play significant roles in uniting people. Major international sports events like the Olympics or the World Cup serve as opportunities for nations to come together and share common goals.

tasks.title: Renewable Energy 讲座（3/4 ❌错1）
tasks.transcript: Renewable energy comes from natural processes that are replenished constantly, such as sunlight, wind and water. They're an alternative to fossil fuels, which contribute to greenhouse gases and global warming. One of the most widely used forms of renewable energy is solar power. You might have seen solar panels on rooftops of private homes or small buildings that convert sunlight into electricity. These panels can last for decades. Obviously, they wouldn't work in places that are cloudy or rainy most of the year. Even in places with plenty of sunlight, no energy is produced at night. This means that you'll need to store energy for later use. But this requires batteries to be connected to solar panels. And these batteries can be expensive. Wind is another common renewable energy source. Wind turbines are large structures with blades that spin when the wind blows. They're typically installed in open areas like farmland and coastal regions. Why are they rare in residential areas? Well, when the blades of wind turbines slice through the air, they produce a swishing or whooshing sound. The faster the blades, the louder it gets. Imagine living near a wind turbine. Unlike solar panels, wind turbines require lots of maintenance. Oil changes, blade inspections, mechanical repairs. A lot needs to be done on a regular basis. Don't forget that some wind farms are located offshore in the open sea. Think about the extra expenses needed to reach these farms and the harsh conditions that need to be overcome.

options.A: To explain why they are not usually found in residential areas

options.C: To explain how technicians know a turbine needs maintenance

tasks.title: Bird Migration 讲座（2/4 ❌错2）
tasks.transcript: Let's talk a bit about bird migration. Migratory birds travel vast distances between their breeding and wintering grounds, often covering thousands of miles. These journeys are driven by the need to find suitable habitats with adequate food supplies and favorable climate conditions. One of the most remarkable aspects of migration is a bird's ability to navigate accurately over such long distances. Birds use a variety of navigational cues, such as the position of the sun, stars, and, incredibly, Earth's magnetic field. Certain bird species have a special protein in their eyes that allows them to see magnetic fields, and this helps them stay on course. Migratory birds play key roles in ecosystems by dispersing seeds and controlling pests, so their decline can cause imbalances throughout food webs. Of course, a migration over hundreds or even thousands of miles will be fraught with risk. Obvious dangers include harsh weather conditions, predators, and the risk of exhaustion and starvation. Less obviously, human activities also pose significant threats to migratory birds. Habitat destruction, pollution, and climate change have led to a decline in many migratory bird populations. At night, light pollution can disorient birds that navigate by the stars, causing them to become lost or collide with buildings.

tasks.title: Gut Microbiome 讲座（2/4 ❌错2）
tasks.transcript: Have you ever experienced a sudden change in mood after you eat a meal? It's plausible that your gut microbiome played a role in that emotional shift. Okay, so the microbiome is an intricate network of bacteria, fungi, and various other microorganisms. Trillions of these tiny entities make up your microbiome. In recent years, our understanding of the microbiome has greatly expanded. We used to think of microbes primarily as pathogens, but we now recognize that microbes play an essential role in our health. Right, so these microbes are integral to your health, influencing your immune system. A diverse microbiome acts as an implicit defense mechanism, strengthening the immune system against potential pathogens that could be harmful. And recent studies underscore the significance of a gut microbiome in how our bodies respond to infections and even in shaping emotions. Microbes in the gut synthesize neurotransmitters, chemical messengers, such as serotonin. And you probably know serotonin, right? Serotonin is a neurotransmitter that influences our emotional state. This interaction between the gut and the central nervous system reveals a dynamic relationship. You could even think of it like a finely tuned orchestra. As research into the microbiome advances, the possibility of manipulating gut microbes as a medical treatment, from addressing autoimmune conditions to enhancing mental health, becomes increasingly likely. So you might even imagine a scenario where doctors prescribe personalized probiotic regimens tailored specifically to your unique microbiome. This would be a fundamental change that could redefine personalized medicine.

tasks.title: Lean Manufacturing 讲座（2/4 ❌错2）
tasks.transcript: Let's talk about lean manufacturing and its impact on efficiency in production processes. Lean manufacturing is a systematic approach to minimizing waste within a manufacturing system while maximizing productivity. While the methodology has been adopted by many companies worldwide, it was developed by a Japanese carmaker in the mid 20th century. But its roots can actually be traced to the supermarket. In the 1950s, Japanese engineers observed that supermarkets in the United States only restocked items as customers purchased them, maintaining just enough inventory to meet demand. This idea of just in time inventory management became a core principle of lean manufacturing. By identifying and removing excess inventory and eliminating other inefficiencies, companies could reduce costs and increase their overall productivity. Another important aspect of lean manufacturing is continuous improvement, often referred to as kaizen. This involves constantly seeking ways to enhance processes, products and services. Companies at all levels are encouraged to contribute ideas for improvement, fostering a culture of innovation and teamwork. Lean manufacturing also emphasizes the importance of value from the customer's perspective. Companies focus on producing goods that meet customer needs and expectations, ensuring that each step in the production process adds value rather than unnecessary complexity. As you might imagine, implementing lean manufacturing requires a shift in organizational culture. Resistance to change and difficulty in sustaining improvements can get in the way. That said, companies that successfully adopt lean practices experience increased efficiency, reduced costs and higher customer satisfaction.

options.B: Some cultures do not require much improvement

options.D: If lean practices are implemented, the culture will follow

options.C: Outlines the stages of putting lean into practice

senses.gloss: 适应（生物/生理对环境的调整）
senses.logic: ad-「朝向」+ apt「合适」→ 使自身变得合适
senses.en: The thick fur of polar bears is an adaptation to extreme cold.
senses.zh: 北极熊的厚毛是对极寒环境的一种适应。

senses.logic: 把原作调整成另一种媒介的合适形态
senses.en: The film is a faithful adaptation of the novel.
senses.zh: 这部电影是对那部小说的忠实改编。

wordbank.ety: 拉丁 ad-（朝向）+ aptare（使合适）→ 古义「使适配」，18世纪才指生物对环境的适应
wordbank.ph: 重音在第三音节 -ta-；/æ/ 开口音，注意不要把 adaptation 读成 adaption（也常见但属省略拼写）
wordbank.tip: 想到「adapt（适应）+ 后缀」——动物 adapt，得到 adaptation。

xex.en: Adaptation is the key to survival in a changing climate.
xex.zh: 适应是在不断变化的气候中生存的关键。

xex.en: These plants show remarkable adaptation to drought.
xex.zh: 这些植物展现出对干旱的非凡适应能力。

syn.note: 偏「小步调整」，adaptation 更强调整体、长期或进化层面的适应
偏「人为改动」，adaptation 常指自然/自发的适应

wordbank.nu: 生物学术语中 adaptation 指可遗传的进化适应；日常语境「适应新工作」常说 adapt (v.) 而非用名词。

wordbank.zh: adj. 自身免疫的；n. 自身免疫（疾病，非正式）
wordbank.core: 免疫系统认错了目标，把自己的身体当成敌人来攻击。

senses.gloss: 自身免疫的（免疫系统攻击自身组织）
senses.logic: auto-「自己」+ immune「免疫」→ 对自己产生免疫反应
senses.en: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune disease.
senses.zh: 类风湿关节炎是一种自身免疫性疾病。

wordbank.ety: 希腊 autos（自己）+ 拉丁 immunis（免除义务、不受影响的）→ 现代医学术语，20世纪中期确立
wordbank.ph: auto- 读 /ˈɔːtoʊ/；immune 重音在第二音节 -mune，字母 u 读 /juː/
wordbank.tip: auto- 是「自己」（automobile 自动车），immune 是「免疫」，合起来=「自己打自己」。

xex.en: Autoimmune disorders occur when the body attacks its own cells.
xex.zh: 当身体攻击自身细胞时，就会发生自身免疫性疾病。

xex.en: Researchers are studying why autoimmune responses become overactive.
xex.zh: 研究人员正在研究为何自身免疫反应会变得过度活跃。

syn.note: 偏描述性术语，指免疫细胞对自身抗原反应，不如 autoimmune 通用

wordbank.nu: autoimmune 是形容词，常修饰 disease/response/disorder；作名词时通常说 autoimmune disease 而非单用 autoimmune。

wordbank.zh: n. 理解（力）；阅读理解（测试）
wordbank.core: 把零散的信息「抓在一起」，从字面看到完整的意思。

senses.logic: com-「共同」+ prehendere「抓住」→ 把意思全抓在手里
senses.en: The article is beyond my comprehension.
senses.zh: 这篇文章超出了我的理解范围。

senses.logic: 学校语境下专门指对文本理解的测试
senses.en: We had a reading comprehension test this morning.
senses.zh: 今天早上我们做了一次阅读理解测试。

wordbank.ety: 拉丁 comprehendere（抓住、握住）→ 中世纪英语转指「心智上抓住、理解」
wordbank.ph: 重音在 -hen-；compre 中的 e 读 /ɪ/ 弱化音，注意别把 -hen- 读成 /hen/ 而应 /hen/ 弱读为 /hɪ/ 的变体，实际标准音 /ˌkɒmprɪˈhenʃn/
wordbank.tip: com- 一起 + prehend 抓 = 把信息一把抓住 → 理解。

xex.en: Listening comprehension improves with daily practice.
xex.zh: 听力理解通过日常练习得以提高。

xex.en: The text is too dense for quick comprehension.
xex.zh: 这篇文章太密集，难以快速理解。

syn.note: 最通用、日常；comprehension 偏正式、常用于教育/测试语境
偏「抓住要领」的瞬间把握，comprehension 指完整深层的理解

wordbank.nu: TOEFL 中 reading comprehension 是固定搭配；comprehension 侧重理解的过程/能力，comprehension of + 名词。

wordbank.zh: n. 建造；建筑物；结构；解释（对意义的构建）
wordbank.core: 把材料或想法「垒在一起」，从无到有搭出有结构的东西。

senses.logic: con-「共同」+ struere「堆叠」→ 一起堆起来
senses.en: The bridge is still under construction.
senses.zh: 这座桥仍在施工中。

senses.logic: 被建出来的那个「结构体」
senses.en: The construction of the sentence is unusual.
senses.zh: 这个句子的结构很不寻常。

senses.logic: 抽象地把观点「搭建」成体系
senses.en: Each culture has its own construction of reality.
senses.zh: 每种文化都有自己对现实的建构。

wordbank.ety: 拉丁 construere（堆叠、建造）→ con- + struere；经法语 construction 进入英语
wordbank.ph: 重音在 -struc-；-tion 读 /ʃn/；字母组合 str 连读，勿漏 /s/
wordbank.tip: struct 词根=「搭建」，structure（结构）和 construction（建造）同源。

xex.en: The construction of the subway took five years.
xex.zh: 这条地铁的建设花了五年时间。

xex.en: Grammar studies the construction of sentences.
xex.zh: 语法研究句子的构造。

syn.note: 既可指动作也可指建筑实体；construction 更正式、偏过程与工程
偏指「结构」本身，construction 强调「建造」的动作或过程

wordbank.nu: under construction（正在施工）为固定搭配；作「解释」义时偏学术，常搭配 a social/cultural construction。

wordbank.zh: n. 松饼（英式，多孔发酵面饼，常烤后涂黄油）
wordbank.core: 英式早餐里那张满是蜂窝小孔、越烤越香的面饼。

senses.logic: 来自古英语 crumpled「卷曲的」→ 边缘微卷、质地松软的饼
senses.en: We toasted crumpets and spread them with butter.
senses.zh: 我们烤了松饼，并涂上黄油。

wordbank.ety: 中古英语 crompid（卷曲的），与 crumple（起皱）同源，指饼面因发酵起泡而凹凸不平
wordbank.ph: 字母 u 读 /ʌ/；词尾 -et 读 /ɪt/ 弱读；首字母 c 读 /k/
wordbank.tip: 想象 crumpet 表面像 crumple（起皱）的纸一样布满小坑。

xex.en: Crumpets are best eaten hot with melting butter.
xex.zh: 松饼趁热吃、配上融化的黄油最好。

xex.en: He ate two crumpets with tea for breakfast.
xex.zh: 他早餐配茶吃了两块松饼。

syn.note: 英式 muffin 偏面包质地、对半切烤；crumpet 更软、表面有孔，两者外形口感都不同

wordbank.nu: 英式食物，美式语境不常用；复数为 crumpets。注意不要与 pancake（平底锅煎饼）混淆。

wordbank.zh: v. 使迷失方向；使困惑、使不知所措
wordbank.core: 把人脑中的「方向感」拔掉，让人分不清东西南北、也理不清头绪。

senses.logic: dis-「去除」+ orient「定向、朝向」→ 拿走方向
senses.en: The thick fog disoriented the hikers.
senses.zh: 浓雾使徒步者迷失了方向。

senses.logic: 从空间迷失引申到心理上的「找不到北」
senses.en: The sudden change of plan disoriented everyone.
senses.zh: 计划的突然改变让所有人都摸不着头脑。

wordbank.ety: 法语 désorienter：dis-（去除）+ orient（东方、朝向）→ 失去朝向；orient 原义「使朝向东方」
wordbank.ph: 重音在 -or-（读 /ɔː/）；dis- 前缀读 /dɪs/，注意美式 /ˈɔːrient/，英式 orient 常读 /ˈɒrient/
wordbank.tip: orient 是「朝向东方」= 确定方向；dis- 否定 → 失去方向。

xex.en: The maze of narrow streets disoriented the tourists.
xex.zh: 迷宫般的狭窄街道让游客迷失了方向。

xex.en: Waking in a strange room can be disorienting.
xex.zh: 在陌生的房间醒来会让人感到晕头转向。

syn.note: 偏「搞混、弄乱思维」；disorient 特指空间/方向感的迷失，更具体
偏「完全懵掉」的困惑，程度更强，与方向无关

wordbank.nu: disoriented（形容词，感到迷失）比动词更常用；disorient 及物，宾语常是人。

wordbank.zh: n. 壮举、功绩、技艺成就
wordbank.core: 一件凭本事「做出来」的、值得夸耀的难事。

senses.gloss: 壮举、功绩（需要技巧或勇气的成就）
senses.logic: 拉丁 factum「做成的事」→ 古法语 fait → 英语 feat
senses.en: Landing on the moon was an astonishing feat.
senses.zh: 登月是一项惊人的壮举。

wordbank.ety: 古法语 fait（行为、功绩），源自拉丁 factum「做成的事」，与 fact（事实）同源
wordbank.ph: ea 读长音 /iː/；词尾 -t 发清音 /t/；与 feet（脚）同音，注意拼写区别
wordbank.tip: feat 和 fact 同源——都是「做」出来的东西，feat 是了不起的那个 fact。

xex.en: Climbing Everest in winter is an incredible feat.
xex.zh: 冬季攀登珠穆朗玛峰是一项难以置信的壮举。

xex.en: The bridge is a remarkable feat of engineering.
xex.zh: 这座桥是一项了不起的工程壮举。

syn.note: 偏「取得的成果/成就」，通用；feat 强调「难度、了不起」，更具惊叹色彩
偏「完成的事项」，语气平和；feat 突出「非凡、艰难」

wordbank.nu: 常用搭配 a feat of（…的壮举），如 a feat of engineering/endurance；单数可数名词。

wordbank.core: 远古生物留下的石质「印痕」，被时间挖出来。

senses.logic: 拉丁 fossilis「被挖出的」→ 从地里挖出的古生物遗骸
senses.en: The museum has a complete fossil of a dinosaur.
senses.zh: 博物馆里有一具完整的恐龙化石。

wordbank.ety: 拉丁 fossilis（被挖出的），源自 fodere（挖掘）；18世纪起专指石化古生物遗骸
wordbank.ph: o 读短音 /ɒ/（英式）；词尾 -il 读 /l/ 不发音字母 i；美式 o 略偏 /ɑː/
wordbank.tip: fossil 来自「挖」（fodere）——化石都是被从地里「挖」出来的。

xex.en: Fossils provide evidence of ancient life forms.
xex.zh: 化石为远古生命形态提供了证据。

xex.en: This fossil is over a hundred million years old.
xex.zh: 这块化石已有一亿多年的历史。

syn.note: 偏「遗骸、遗迹」，范围更广；fossil 特指石化的古生物遗存

wordbank.nu: fossil fuel（化石燃料）是常见固定搭配，指煤、石油、天然气；注意此义与「化石」本义相关但已引申。

wordbank.zh: n. 平底煎锅（扁平的烤盘/铁板）；v. 用平底锅煎烤
wordbank.core: 一块平摊的热铁板，面糊倒上去就成饼。

senses.gloss: 平底煎锅、铁板（用于烙饼/煎烤）
senses.logic: 古法语 gredil（格栅）→ 早期指带格架的烤架，后指平板煎锅
senses.en: She poured the batter onto the hot griddle.
senses.zh: 她把面糊倒到滚烫的平底煎锅上。

wordbank.ety: 古法语 gredil/greil（格栅、烤架），源自拉丁 craticula（小格栅）；词义从「格架」演变为「平板铁盘」
wordbank.ph: 字母组合 -ddle 读 /dl/，中间的 d 只发一个音；首字母 g 读 /ɡ/
wordbank.tip: griddle 和 grid（格栅）同源，早期就是带格子的烤架，后来变成光滑平板。

xex.en: Cook the pancakes on a greased griddle.
xex.zh: 在涂了油的平底锅上煎薄饼。

xex.en: The chef warmed tortillas on the griddle.
xex.zh: 厨师在铁板上加热玉米饼。

syn.note: 偏「带柄煎锅」，通常有边；griddle 是平坦、常无边的大铁板，用于烙饼类
最通用的「锅」；griddle 特指平底、常用于 pancake/crumpet 的平板

wordbank.nu: 美式早餐场景常用（griddle 上做 pancake）；英式语境较少见。注意 g 不读 /dʒ/。

wordbank.zh: adj. 免疫的；不受影响的；豁免的
wordbank.core: 体内有一道「挡箭牌」，让病原或影响近不了身。

senses.gloss: 免疫的（对疾病有抵抗力）
senses.logic: 拉丁 immunis「免于公共服务/义务」→ 引申为免于疾病侵害
senses.en: Vaccines help people become immune to the virus.
senses.zh: 疫苗帮助人们对病毒产生免疫力。

senses.logic: 从「免于疾病」引申为「免于任何影响或责任」
senses.en: No one is immune to criticism.
senses.zh: 没有人能免于批评。

wordbank.ety: 拉丁 immunis（免于公共义务），由 in-（不）+ munus（义务、服务）构成；19世纪引入医学「免疫」义
wordbank.ph: 重音在第二音节；i 读 /ɪ/，mune 中的 u 读 /juː/；注意与 immune 相关词 immunity 重音不同
wordbank.tip: im-（不）+ munus（义务）= 不用「交税/服役」= 被免除 → 引申为「免疫」。

xex.en: The immune system defends the body against infection.
xex.zh: 免疫系统保护身体免受感染。

xex.en: Some people seem immune to cold weather.
xex.zh: 有些人似乎对寒冷天气毫不在意。

syn.note: 偏「有抵抗力的」，可用于物理/化学；immune 强调生物免疫机制，也可指「完全免疫」
偏「被豁免（责任/税收）」，与 immune 的「免疫」义不同，仅在「豁免」义上接近

wordbank.nu: 常见搭配 immune to + 名词（对…免疫/不受影响）；immune system（免疫系统）为高频固定搭配。

wordbank.zh: n. 持续改善（源自日本的持续改进理念，尤用于管理/制造）
wordbank.core: 不追求一步到位，而是靠「每天一点点」的持续改进积少成多。

senses.gloss: 持续改善（日本管理理念）
senses.logic: 日语 改善（kai「改」+ zen「善」）→ 改而善之、不断变好
senses.en: The factory adopted kaizen to reduce waste.
senses.zh: 这家工厂采用持续改善的方法来减少浪费。

wordbank.ety: 日语「改善」（かいぜん），由 改（改）+ 善（好）构成；二战后随丰田生产体系传入西方管理学
wordbank.ph: kai 读 /kaɪ/（如 kite 的 kai），zen 读 /zen/；重音在首音节；按日语罗马音直读即可
wordbank.tip: 「改 + 善」= 改了更好；kaizen 就是「越来越好」的日语版。

xex.en: Kaizen focuses on small, continuous improvements.
xex.zh: 持续改善专注于微小而不断的改进。

xex.en: Many companies hold kaizen workshops for employees.
xex.zh: 许多公司为员工举办持续改善工作坊。

syn.note: kaizen 的英文本义直译，通用；kaizen 是更简洁、带日本管理文化色彩的专业术语

wordbank.nu: 商务/管理学专用术语，通常不加冠词复数，作不可数名词；首字母常小写。

wordbank.zh: v. 倾斜、倚靠；adj. 瘦的、精简的、高效的
wordbank.core: 身体或组织「削掉多余」，往一个方向靠，也往更高效处靠。

senses.logic: 古英语 hleonian「倾斜、倚靠」
senses.en: She leaned against the wall.
senses.zh: 她靠在墙上。

senses.logic: 从「倾斜」的细长感引申为「不胖、无多余脂肪」
senses.en: He is tall and lean.
senses.zh: 他又高又瘦。

senses.gloss: 精简的、高效的（adj.，指组织/生产）
senses.logic: 从「瘦」引申为「无冗余、效率高」
senses.en: The company runs a lean operation.
senses.zh: 这家公司实行精简高效的运营。

wordbank.ety: 古英语 hleonian（倾斜、倚靠）；形容词义由「细长、倾斜」引申而来；lean production（精益生产）来自丰田模式
wordbank.ph: ea 读长音 /iː/；与 learned 无关，lean 的过去式是 leaned 或 leant（英式）
wordbank.tip: 一个人「靠」在墙上是 lean，一个「瘦」组织没有赘肉也是 lean——都是去掉多余。

xex.en: Lean manufacturing eliminates unnecessary steps.
xex.zh: 精益制造消除了不必要的步骤。

xex.en: The tower leans slightly to one side.
xex.zh: 这座塔微微向一侧倾斜。

syn.note: 偏「苗条、纤细」，多形容人；lean 强调「无脂肪、精瘦」，也可形容组织精简
偏「修长优雅」；lean 更强调瘦而无赘肉，且有「高效」引申义
最通用「薄的/瘦的」；lean 含「健康结实」的正面色彩

wordbank.nu: lean 作形容词时与 manufacturing/production 搭配表「精益（生产）」，是管理学高频词；作动词常用于 lean on（倚靠/依赖）。

wordbank.zh: adj. 磁性的；有吸引力的
wordbank.core: 像磁铁一样，能把东西「吸」过来——物理上吸铁，人格上吸人。

senses.logic: 来自 magnet（磁铁），源自希腊 magnēs（马格尼西亚的石头）
senses.en: The magnetic field protects Earth from radiation.
senses.zh: 磁场保护地球免受辐射。

senses.logic: 从「磁吸」引申为「吸引人的魅力」
senses.en: She has a magnetic personality.
senses.zh: 她有一种极具吸引力的个性。

wordbank.ety: 希腊 magnēs lithos（马格尼西亚之石，一种天然磁铁矿）→ 拉丁 magnes → 英语 magnet，再加 -ic 成形容词
wordbank.ph: 重音在 -net-（读 /net/）；g 读 /ɡ/；注意与 magic 无关，勿把 g 读成 /dʒ/
wordbank.tip: 古希腊人在 Magnesia 发现会吸铁的石头，所以磁铁就叫 magnet——磁性的就是 magnetic。

xex.en: A compass needle points north because of Earth's magnetic field.
xex.zh: 由于地球磁场，指南针的指针指向北方。

xex.en: His magnetic charm drew a large audience.
xex.zh: 他那极具魅力的风采吸引了大批听众。

syn.note: 偏「外表/气质吸引人」；magnetic 强调一种强烈的、无法抗拒的吸引力，更具比喻色彩
偏「领袖魅力、感召力」；magnetic 更强调「吸住人」的吸引力

wordbank.nu: magnetic field（磁场）、magnetic personality（有磁性的个性）都是高频搭配。

wordbank.zh: n. 制造业、制造；adj. 制造的
wordbank.core: 用手（manu-）把原料「做」成商品的那套工业流水。

senses.logic: manu「手」+ fact「做」→ 最初指「手工制作」，后指机器化生产
senses.en: Manufacturing is the backbone of the economy.
senses.zh: 制造业是经济的支柱。

wordbank.ety: 拉丁 manu（手）+ factura（制作）→ 中世纪拉丁 manufactura「手工制作」；工业革命后转指工厂化生产
wordbank.ph: 重音在 -fac-（读 /fæk/）；manu- 读 /ˌmænju/，u 读 /ju/；注意 -ring 读 /rɪŋ/
wordbank.tip: manu 手 + fact 做 = 最早是「手做」，现在指「工厂造」。

xex.en: The region relies heavily on manufacturing for jobs.
xex.zh: 该地区在就业上高度依赖制造业。

xex.en: Robots are transforming modern manufacturing.
xex.zh: 机器人正在改变现代制造业。

syn.note: 偏「生产」的广义概念；manufacturing 特指工厂、机械化的「制造」
偏「装配、制作」，多用于工程/精密件；manufacturing 更宏观、指整个产业

wordbank.nu: manufacturing 常作不可数名词，作定语修饰 industry/sector/plant；动词形式为 manufacture。

wordbank.zh: n. 微生物组（生活在特定环境中的微生物及其基因的集合）
wordbank.core: 住在你体内外、肉眼看不见的亿万微生命，组成的那个「隐形生态系统」。

senses.gloss: 微生物组（尤指人体内的微生物群落）
senses.logic: micro-「微小」+ bio-「生命」+ -ome「集合、整体」→ 微生命的总集合
senses.en: The gut microbiome plays a role in digestion.
senses.zh: 肠道微生物组在消化中发挥作用。

wordbank.ety: 现代合成词：micro-（微小）+ biome（生物群落），biome 又由 bio（生命）+ -ome（整体、集合）构成，21世纪初流行
wordbank.ph: 重音在 -bi-（读 /baɪ/）；micro- 读 /ˌmaɪkrəʊ/，biome 读 /ˈbaɪəʊm/；注意 o 之间的连读
wordbank.tip: micro 微小 + biome 生物群落 = 一个「微观的生物群」，就是 microbiome。

xex.en: Diet can change the composition of the gut microbiome.
xex.zh: 饮食可以改变肠道微生物组的构成。

xex.en: Scientists study the human microbiome to understand health.
xex.zh: 科学家研究人体微生物组以理解健康。

syn.note: 偏指微生物「群落本身」（the microbes），microbiome 还包括其基因和所处环境，范围更广

wordbank.nu: 现代生物医学高频词，常搭配 gut/human/skin microbiome；注意与 microbiota 的区别（microbiome 含基因组与环境）。

wordbank.zh: 名词：迁移；移居；（动物的）季节性迁徙
wordbank.core: 群体性地从一个地方搬到另一个地方

senses.logic: 由“移动”引申指人口跨地域的长期搬迁
senses.en: Large-scale migration from rural to urban areas transformed the country.
senses.zh: 从农村到城市的大规模人口迁移改变了这个国家。

senses.logic: 引申指鸟类、鱼类等按季节往返移动
senses.en: Bird migration depends on changes in day length and temperature.
senses.zh: 鸟类的迁徙取决于日照时长和温度的变化。

wordbank.ety: 拉丁语 migrare「移动、更换居住地」→ 名词 migratio，本义即“从一个地方移到另一个地方”。
wordbank.ph: 重音在第二音节 grei；结尾 -tion 固定读 /ʃən/，不读 /tɪən/。
wordbank.tip: 想象“移民(migrate)”搬家，migration 就是那场“大搬家”。

xex.en: Climate change is altering the migration routes of many species.
xex.zh: 气候变化正在改变许多物种的迁徙路线。

xex.en: Migration has been a key driver of cultural exchange throughout history.
xex.zh: 纵观历史，人口迁移一直是文化交流的重要推动力。

syn.note: 泛指移动，中性，不强调跨地域或季节性
强调人或机构的具体搬迁，比 migration 更具体、更偏向一次性

wordbank.nu: 作学术名词常与 mass（大规模）、seasonal（季节性）、route（路线）搭配；特指动物迁徙时不可用 emigration/immigration（那两个只用于人的出入境）。

wordbank.zh: 形容词：迁徙的；迁移的；（动物）季节性迁徙的
wordbank.core: 有“搬家/迁徙”习性的、与迁徙相关的

senses.logic: 由动词 migrate 派生，指有迁徙习性的
senses.en: Migratory birds travel thousands of miles each year.
senses.zh: 候鸟每年飞行数千英里。

senses.gloss: 迁移的、流动的（人口/生活方式）
senses.logic: 引申指人不断移动、不长期定居的
senses.en: The region has a highly migratory workforce.
senses.zh: 该地区有一支高度流动的劳动力队伍。

wordbank.ety: 拉丁语 migrare「移动」+ 形容词后缀 -tory，本义“倾向于移动的”。
wordbank.ph: 重音在第一音节 mi；英式读 /ˈmaɪɡrətri/（省去倒数第二音节的 ə），美式常读四个音节。
wordbank.tip: 记住 migratory bird（候鸟）这个高频搭配就掌握了整词。

xex.en: Many migratory fish return to the same river where they were born to spawn.
xex.zh: 许多洄游鱼类回到它们出生的那条河去产卵。

xex.en: The wetlands provide a crucial stopover for migratory species.
xex.zh: 这些湿地为迁徙物种提供了关键的停歇地。

syn.note: 指游牧、居无定所的（常指人），不限于动物的季节性迁徙

wordbank.nu: 与 migration 同根但词性不同；migratory 多修饰 bird、fish、species、route。

wordbank.zh: 名词：神经递质（神经元之间传递信号的化学物质）
wordbank.core: 神经之间“传话”的化学信使
wordbank.ety: 希腊语 neuron「神经」+ 拉丁 trans「跨过」+ mittere「送」→ 本义“跨过神经间隙传递的东西”。
wordbank.ph: 三个词素拼合，重音落在 transmit 的 mit；neuro- 读 /ˌnʊroʊ-/（英式读 /ˌnjʊə-/）。
wordbank.tip: 拆成 neuro（神经）+ transmitter（发射器/传话者）= 神经间的传话者。

xex.en: Serotonin and dopamine are two well-known neurotransmitters.
xex.zh: 血清素和多巴胺是两种广为人知的神经递质。

xex.en: A shortage of certain neurotransmitters has been linked to depression.
xex.zh: 某些神经递质的缺乏被认为与抑郁症有关。

wordbank.nu: 常以复数出现（neurotransmitters）；记忆时抓住 transmit（传送）这个核心动作。

wordbank.zh: 形容词/副词：离岸的；近海的；海上的；海外的（金融/外包）
wordbank.core: 离开岸边、在近海或海外的

senses.gloss: 近海的、海上的（风电场/钻井）
senses.logic: off（离开）+ shore（岸），指离开岸边在海上
senses.en: Offshore wind farms generate clean electricity.
senses.zh: 海上风电场生产清洁电力。

senses.gloss: 离岸的、海外的（金融/公司）
senses.logic: 由地理意义引申指在本国境外注册经营的
senses.en: The company moved its profits to an offshore account.
senses.zh: 这家公司把利润转移到离岸账户。

wordbank.ety: 古英语 off「离开」+ shore「岸」（中古英语 schore），本义就是“离岸的”。
wordbank.ph: 重音在 shore；作表语/副词常读 /ˌɔːfˈʃɔːr/，作定语修饰名词时也可读 /ˈɔːfʃɔːr/。
wordbank.tip: off（离开）+ shore（海岸）= 离开海岸，一眼可拆。

xex.en: Offshore drilling has raised concerns about marine pollution.
xex.zh: 海上钻井引发了人们对海洋污染的担忧。

xex.en: Offshore outsourcing can reduce labor costs but may affect quality.
xex.zh: 离岸外包可以降低劳动力成本，但可能影响质量。

syn.note: 沿海的、海岸的（在岸上/靠近岸），与 offshore（远离岸）方向相反

wordbank.nu: 修饰 wind farm、drilling 时指“海上”；修饰 account、company、banking 时指“离岸/境外”（常带避税含义）。

wordbank.zh: 形容词：组织的；组织性的；机构方面的
wordbank.core: 与“组织/机构”有关的
wordbank.ety: 希腊语 organon「工具、器官」→ 拉丁 organizare「安排、组织」→ organization → organizational，本义“使各部件像器官一样协调工作”。
wordbank.ph: 重音在 za；结尾 -tional 读 /ʃənəl/，其中的 t 不单独爆破（与 -tion 同规律）。
wordbank.tip: 由 organize（组织）加 -ation 再 -al 层层派生，看到 organization 就认得。

xex.en: Effective leadership requires strong organizational skills.
xex.zh: 有效的领导需要很强的组织能力。

xex.en: The report recommends several organizational changes.
xex.zh: 这份报告建议进行若干组织层面的调整。

syn.note: 机构的、制度化的，更强调已成型的制度/机构；organizational 更强调组织职能

wordbank.nu: 拼写英美差异：美式 organizational，英式 organisational（z/s 之别，同 organize/organise）。

wordbank.zh: 名词：病原体（能引起疾病的微生物）
wordbank.core: 制造疾病的“病源”
wordbank.ety: 希腊语 pathos「痛苦、疾病」+ -gen「产生」→ 本义“产生疾病的东西”。
wordbank.ph: 重音在第一音节 pa；-gen 读 /dʒən/，与 generate、oxygen 中的 -gen 同源同音。
wordbank.tip: path（病，如 pathology 病理学）+ gen（产生）= 产生病的东西。

xex.en: Bacteria, viruses, and fungi can all act as pathogens.
xex.zh: 细菌、病毒和真菌都可能成为病原体。

xex.en: Washing hands is a simple way to reduce exposure to pathogens.
xex.zh: 洗手是减少接触病原体的一种简单方法。

syn.note: 口语常用“病菌/细菌”，非正式；pathogen 是学术/医学正式术语

wordbank.nu: 学术语境指病原微生物；注意与 antibody（抗体）、antigen（抗原）区分。

wordbank.zh: 动词：开拓、开创、率先发展；名词：先驱、开拓者
wordbank.core: 第一个开路的人（或行为）

senses.logic: 由名词“开拓者”动词化，指率先做某领域的事
senses.en: She pioneered a new method for studying the brain.
senses.zh: 她开创了一种研究大脑的新方法。

senses.logic: 本义即“走在前面的人”
senses.en: He was a pioneer of modern aviation.
senses.zh: 他是现代航空的先驱。

wordbank.ety: 法语 pionnier「步兵、先遣工兵」→ 古法语 peonier，源于 peon「步兵」（拉丁 pes「脚」）。先遣工兵走在部队前面开路，故引申为“开拓者”。
wordbank.ph: 重音在第三音节 neer /nɪr/；注意 pioneer 中 o 弱读为 /ə/，不读 /oʊ/。
wordbank.tip: 先遣工兵走最前头开路 → 第一个做的人就是 pioneer。

xex.en: The scientist pioneered research into renewable energy storage.
xex.zh: 这位科学家开创了可再生能源储存的研究。

xex.en: The Wright brothers pioneered powered flight in 1903.
xex.zh: 莱特兄弟在1903年开创了动力飞行。

syn.note: 发起、开始，强调启动一个过程；pioneer 强调做前人未做过的、开辟新领域
名词“开路先锋”，比 pioneer 更形象、更强调开创性

wordbank.nu: 作动词常用被动 be pioneered by；作名词常与 in/of 连用（a pioneer in/of…）。

wordbank.zh: 名词：捕食者；掠食者；肉食动物
wordbank.core: 以捕食其他动物为生的动物

senses.logic: 本义，以其他动物为食
senses.en: Wolves are apex predators in many ecosystems.
senses.zh: 狼在许多生态系统中是顶级捕食者。

senses.logic: 由动物捕食引申指侵害他人的人
senses.en: Online predators target vulnerable children.
senses.zh: 网络上的不法分子把目标对准易受伤害的儿童。

wordbank.ety: 拉丁 praedator「掠夺者」源于 praeda「猎物、战利品」→ 本义“抢夺猎物者”。
wordbank.ph: 重音在第一音节 pre；-tor 结尾读 /tər/（美式 r 卷舌）。
wordbank.tip: pre（抢先）+ 联想到 prey（猎物）：抢在猎物前面下手的，就是 predator。

xex.en: The presence of predators helps control herbivore populations.
xex.zh: 捕食者的存在有助于控制食草动物的数量。

xex.en: Camouflage helps prey avoid being seen by predators.
xex.zh: 伪装帮助猎物避免被捕食者发现。

syn.note: 泛指猎手，可指人；predator 专指以捕食为生的动物或掠食者
食肉动物（按食性分类）；predator 强调捕食行为，二者角度不同

wordbank.nu: 与 prey（猎物）成对记忆；学术写作中 apex/top predator（顶级捕食者）是高频搭配。

wordbank.zh: 名词/形容词：益生菌；益生菌的
wordbank.core: 对生命/健康有益的微生物

senses.logic: 指摄入后有益健康的活菌
senses.en: Yogurt contains probiotics that support gut health.
senses.zh: 酸奶含有支持肠道健康的益生菌。

senses.logic: 修饰含益菌的食品/产品
senses.en: Probiotic supplements have become increasingly popular.
senses.zh: 益生菌补充剂越来越受欢迎。

wordbank.ety: pro-「有利于、支持」+ 希腊语 bios「生命」→ biotic「生命的」，本义“有利于生命的（菌）”，与 antibiotic（抗生命的）相对。
wordbank.ph: 重音在 o（biotic 的 o）；pro- 读 /ˌproʊ-/；与 antibiotic 拼写对照记忆。
wordbank.tip: pro（支持）+ bio（生命）= 支持生命的菌，正好和 anti-biotic（杀生命）相反。

xex.en: Probiotics may help restore the balance of gut bacteria after antibiotics.
xex.zh: 益生菌可能有助于在服用抗生素后恢复肠道菌群的平衡。

xex.en: Fermented foods are a natural source of probiotics.
xex.zh: 发酵食品是益生菌的天然来源。

wordbank.nu: 与 antibiotic（抗生素）对比记忆；常与 gut（肠道）、fermented（发酵的）搭配。

wordbank.zh: 名词：生产力；生产率；产出效率
wordbank.core: 单位投入能产出多少的能力
wordbank.ety: 拉丁 pro「向前」+ ducere「引导、拉出」→ producere「生产」→ productive → productivity，本义“把东西带出来的能力”。
wordbank.ph: 重音在 tiv；注意 productive /prəˈdʌktɪv/ 变 productivity 时重音后移到 /ˌtɪv/。
wordbank.tip: 由 product（产品）联想：造产品的能力就是 productivity。

xex.en: Improved technology can significantly boost worker productivity.
xex.zh: 改进技术可以显著提高工人生产率。

xex.en: Sleep deprivation has a measurable impact on productivity.
xex.zh: 睡眠不足对生产率有明显的影响。

syn.note: 效率（投入产出比），强调不浪费；productivity 强调产出量/生产率

wordbank.nu: 经济学核心词；labor productivity（劳动生产率）是固定搭配。

wordbank.zh: 形容词：心理的；心理学的；精神上的
wordbank.core: 与心灵/精神有关的
wordbank.ety: 希腊语 psyche「灵魂、心灵」+ logos「学说、研究」→ psychology → psychological，本义“关于心灵/精神的”。
wordbank.ph: 重音在 lo（logical 的 lo）；psych- 开头的 p 不发音，读 /saɪ-/。
wordbank.tip: psych- 开头的 p 从不发音，先读 sai（赛），再想到 mind（心灵）。

xex.en: Chronic stress can have serious psychological effects.
xex.zh: 长期压力可能产生严重的心理影响。

xex.en: The study examines the psychological factors behind decision-making.
xex.zh: 这项研究考察了决策背后的心理因素。

syn.note: 精神的、脑力的，更口语通用；psychological 更强调心理学层面、系统化

wordbank.nu: 与 physical（身体的）对照使用；psychological 强调“心理学/精神层面”，mental 更泛指“脑力的”。

wordbank.zh: 动词：补充；重新装满；再补给
wordbank.core: 把用掉的东西重新填满
wordbank.ety: 拉丁 re-「再次」+ plenus「满的」→ 中古法语 replenir「再填满」→ 本义“使重新变满”。
wordbank.ph: 重音在第二音节 plen；re- 读 /rɪ/ 弱读；plen- 中 e 读短音 /e/。
wordbank.tip: re（再次）+ plen（满，如 plenty 富足）= 再次装满。

xex.en: Rain helps replenish groundwater supplies.
xex.zh: 降雨有助于补充地下水供应。

xex.en: The body needs sleep to replenish its energy.
xex.zh: 身体需要睡眠来补充能量。

syn.note: 恢复（原状），强调回到之前状态；replenish 强调把减少的存量补足
再装满，更具体（杯、瓶）；replenish 可用于抽象存量（能量、资源）

wordbank.nu: 常与 supplies、stock、energy、groundwater 等搭配；是可持续/生态话题高频词。

wordbank.zh: 名词：血清素；5-羟色胺（一种神经递质，调节情绪、睡眠、食欲）
wordbank.core: 让人平静、情绪稳定的“快乐”神经递质
wordbank.ety: serum「血清」（拉丁，本义“乳清、浆液”）+ -tonin（由 tonic「强健、张力」造词）→ 因最初从血清中分离、且能引起血管收缩而得名。
wordbank.ph: 重音在 to；sero- 读 /ˌserə-/；结尾 -tonin 中 to 读 /toʊ/。
wordbank.tip: serum（血清）+ tonin（联想到 tone 张力）：从血清里发现、影响“张力”的物质。

xex.en: Low levels of serotonin are associated with depression.
xex.zh: 血清素水平低与抑郁症相关。

xex.en: Exposure to sunlight can increase serotonin production.
xex.zh: 接受阳光照射可以增加血清素的生成。

wordbank.nu: 常与 dopamine（多巴胺）并列出现；两者都是“快乐相关”神经递质，但血清素偏“平静/满足”，多巴胺偏“奖励/动力”。

wordbank.zh: 形容词：陆地的；陆生的；（天文）类地的、地球的
wordbank.core: 属于陆地（而非海洋/天空）的

senses.logic: 由“地/土”引申指陆地上生活或发生的
senses.en: Terrestrial animals evolved from marine ancestors.
senses.zh: 陆生动物由海洋祖先演化而来。

senses.logic: 引申指像地球一样的岩石行星
senses.en: Mars is a terrestrial planet.
senses.zh: 火星是一颗类地行星。

wordbank.ety: 拉丁 terra「土地、大地」→ terrestris「属于陆地的」→ 本义“与大地相关的”。
wordbank.ph: 重音在 res；第一个音节 te 读 /tə/ 弱读；结尾 -trial 读 /triəl/。
wordbank.tip: terra（土地，如 territory 领土、Mediterranean 地中海）= 跟“地”有关。

xex.en: Terrestrial ecosystems include forests, grasslands, and deserts.
xex.zh: 陆地生态系统包括森林、草原和沙漠。

xex.en: The study compares marine and terrestrial food webs.
xex.zh: 这项研究比较了海洋和陆地的食物网。

syn.note: 陆上的、以陆地为基地的，更口语；terrestrial 是学术正式词

wordbank.nu: 常与 marine（海洋的）、aquatic（水生的）对照；天文学中 terrestrial planet（类地行星）是术语。

wordbank.zh: 名词：涡轮机；透平机（靠流体推动旋转的机器）
wordbank.core: 靠气流/水流推动旋转的“风车”式机器
wordbank.ety: 拉丁 turbo「旋涡、陀螺、旋转」→ 法语 turbine → 本义“旋转的东西”。
wordbank.ph: 重音在第一音节 tur；结尾 -bine 读 /baɪn/（不读 /biːn/）；tur 读 /tɜːr/。
wordbank.tip: 联想 turbo（涡轮增压）和 tornado（龙卷风，同源“旋转”），都是转动的。

xex.en: Wind turbines convert kinetic energy into electricity.
xex.zh: 风力涡轮机把动能转化为电能。

xex.en: The power plant's turbines are driven by steam.
xex.zh: 这家发电厂的涡轮机由蒸汽驱动。

wordbank.nu: wind turbine（风力发电机）、gas/steam turbine（燃气/蒸汽轮机）是高频搭配。
